planting.note: Set out container-grown stock in spring along the landward edge of marsh or dune swale habitat; established plants need no supplemental irrigation and tolerate brackish, salt-sprayed sites unsuited to most garden shrubs.

directions: Carolina wolfberry is a thorny, sprawling shrub of salt marsh edges and maritime forest margins along the Atlantic and Gulf coasts, including the barrier islands of Georgia and South Carolina, where it grows in brackish, salt-sprayed soil that excludes most woody competitors. Its narrow, fleshy gray-green leaves and small lavender star-shaped flowers give way to bright red, elongated berries closely related to the cultivated Asian goji berry. Grow in full sun in well-drained sandy or loamy soil at the transition between marsh and maritime thicket, where it forms a dense, spiny, wildlife-friendly screen that needs little care once rooted in. It tolerates periodic tidal inundation and salt spray far better than conventional hedge or screening shrubs.
